pr_title: fix(rust, python): Reused input series in rolling_apply should not be orderly

issue_context.title: Wrong results for rolling_apply, when using min() as apply function.
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2], "b": [0, 1, 11.0, 7, 4, 2, 3, 8]})
df.with_columns(
    pl.col('b').cast(pl.Float64)
    .rolling_apply(lambda s: s.min(), window_size=3, min_periods=2)
    .over('a').alias('min')
    )
```


### Issue description

The output of above syntax is below, which is obviously wrong. 
<html>
<body>

1 | 1.0 | 0.0

2 | 4.0 | null
2 | 2.0 | 4.0

<!--EndFragment-->
</body>

### Expected behavior

While using this rolling_min, the result is right.
```python
df.with_columns([pl.col('b').rolling_min(window_size=3, min_periods=2).over('a').alias('min')])
```

comments:
I believe the culprit is the reused input param(series) for apply function. Some of its states have not been cleared per-invoke. 
Fix is coming soon.

review_comments:
We reuse the following `series` to avoid re-allocation.

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/9bfa5b6db9b112328c657651c2def6543ae46473/crates/polars-core/src/chunked_array/ops/rolling_window.rs#L93-L94

But it sometimes be `Ascending`. Because when we computed its size, we went to the following branch:

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/9bfa5b6db9b112328c657651c2def6543ae46473/crates/polars-core/src/chunked_array/ops/chunkops.rs#L77-L79

It will not be unset even after re-compute size. This will affect subsequent function call. For safety reasons, I chose to reset all the states before each function call. I'm not sure if this is the most suitable approach, WDYT?
This is indeed the way to go. Only the `clear_settings` should be before the `compute_len()`. As `compute_len` sets sorted info.
Ah, that's a foolish mistake, I messed up their order. :)
